messages:
alex: Spike idea: instead of duplicating hedged calls, what if edge multiplexes similar read requests into a single upstream call and fans results back? Pros: token savings, fewer upstream calls. Cons: side-effects, resume complexity for streams.

jia: Multiplexing is tempting but we must be strict about side-effects. If we don't carry per-subrequest idempotency markers, we risk duplicating writes. My preference: default-only-read; teams opt-in for anything else and handle idempotency upstream.

matt: Implementation tradeoffs: adding per-subrequest headers (X-Sub-Id, X-Resume-V1) is doable but increases header cardinality and trace complexity. Could make it opt-in per route and off by default.

irene: Streaming resume is the hard part. If upstream returns partial token streams then aborts, each logical request needs a resume checkpoint (kv-cache index or token offset). So the edge must track per-sub checkpoint even while coalesced. That increases memory over the coalesce window.
alex: Prototype notes: coalesce_window_ms=12, keep a tiny in-memory struct mapping sub_id -> {prompt_len, resume_idx, client_conn}. On merge we build a combined payload and attach metadata header with the sub_id list. Upstream agreed to echo back per-sub offsets in a trailer.
jia: Operational concerns: (1) memory spikes during bursts, (2) billing attribution. For (2) we can initially split tokens proportionally by prompt length; ideally upstream returns per-sub token counts.
matt: Also add safety gates: only enable multiplexing when p95 upstream latency > threshold and coalesce_qps > min. Otherwise overhead isn't worth it.
irene: Failure handling: if upstream aborts with partial data and doesn't return per-sub checkpoints, we should fail all subrequests to avoid inconsistent partial state. If it returns checkpoints, we surface them to clients as resume tokens.
alex: Metrics I propose: coalesce_attempts, coalesce_merged_count, coalesce_mem_bytes, coalesce_fallbacks, coalesced_token_split_histogram, per_sub_resume_tokens_issued. We'll export these from the edge console.
matt: Also add a circuit: if coalesce_mem_bytes > threshold OR coalesce_fallbacks_rate > X in last minute, flip route to passthrough for T seconds. Prevents repeated memory storms.
jia: Small UX: opt-in headers should be X-Sub-Id and X-Resume-Mode with allowed values {none, lightweight, full}. Document the semantics clearly.

edge-bot: deploy: edge/proxy/multiplex-v0.1 -> succeeded in staging (2025-04-02T02:20:01Z)

irene: Can someone post a minimal curl example for the read route so I can run a load job?
alex: Example for embeddings route: 

curl -X POST https://edge.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/multiplex \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"hello","sub_id":"s1"}'

alex: In my local stress test (concurrency 250, 1s bursts) multiplexing reduced upstream calls by ~20% but mem spiked; the circuit fallback prevented tail events. I'll open a short RFC with config knobs, headers, and metric names. Thanks for the feedback.
